title: Campaigns: governed workflow and statuses
summary: How a campaign goes from draft through review and approval to sending, who may do each step, and what every status means.

body.text: Campaigns are bulk emails or text messages to a group of your customers. They live under **Marketing → Campaigns**. Creating a campaign saves a draft straight away; nothing is sent until the campaign has been reviewed, approved and then queued or scheduled.

The figures at the top count **Drafts**, **Awaiting review**, **Scheduled** and **Live delivery**. Filter the list with **Search campaign or objective**, **All statuses** and **All channels**, then **Apply filters**. Each row shows the campaign's status, audience, how many were sent, delivery, opens, clicks and conversions. **Audiences**, **Templates** and **Create campaign** are at the top.
Each step has its own permission, in the **Marketing** group under **Settings → Team & roles**, so the person who writes a campaign need not be the one who approves or sends it:

rows: Edit campaign drafts and requested changes
Pause queued or sending campaigns, Cancel scheduled or in-flight campaigns, Retry eligible campaign delivery failures, Archive completed or cancelled campaigns

body.text: The person who submitted a campaign can't approve it. A second person always checks it.

rows: Submitted. Waiting for a reviewer to approve it or ask for changes.
Sent back with a note. Edit it and submit again.
Ready to send now or schedule.
Being sent, in batches, in the background.
Nothing more is sent until someone resumes it.
Finished. Any messages that couldn't be delivered stay listed with the reason.
Sending stopped because of a problem.

body.text: There is no way to send a campaign without review and approval. Customers who have opted out or withdrawn consent are left out when each message is sent, not just when the campaign was planned.

title: Campaigns: create, review, approve and launch
summary: Write a campaign, pass its checks, have it approved, then send it now or schedule it — and pause, cancel or retry while it sends.

items: On **Marketing → Campaigns**, click **Create campaign**.
Type the **Campaign name**, choose the **Channel** (**Email** or **SMS**) and type the **Objective**.
Click **Create and open editor**. The draft is saved; nothing is sent from this screen.

body.text: The editor saves your changes by itself a moment after you stop typing; the top shows **Saving…**, **Saved** or **Unsaved changes**, and **Save draft** saves straight away.

rows: **Campaign name**, **Objective**, **Offer**, **Landing page**, **CTA label** and **CTA URL** (the button), **Budget**, **Target leads**, **Target revenue**, **Success metric** and **Internal notes**. Budget and target revenue are typed in your currency, e.g. 2500.50.
The tracking tags added to your links (**UTM source**, **medium**, **campaign**, **content**, **term**) and the **Attribution window (days)**. Missing tags are filled in for you when someone clicks.

**Who receives it** — choose one of your saved audiences (build them under **Marketing → Audiences**). A campaign without a saved audience can't pass the check or be scheduled. The exact list of recipients is worked out and fixed when the approved campaign is scheduled or queued.
For email: **Subject**, **Preheader**, the email itself and a **Plain-text fallback**. For SMS: the **Message**.

items: Click **Review** on the campaign. The **QA checklist** lists anything wrong as **Error** (must be fixed) or **Warning** (worth checking).
When there are no errors, click **Submit for review**.
A reviewer opens the same page and either types the **Required changes** and clicks **Request changes**, or adds an **Approval note** and clicks **Approve campaign**.
**Send now** → **Queue campaign**: fixes the recipient list and starts sending in the background.
Set the **Schedule date and time** and click **Schedule campaign** to send later.

body.text: Check the audience and the content preview before you queue or schedule. Once messages have gone out they can't be called back.

The campaign's page shows **Recipients**, **Delivery**, **Engagement** and **Conversions**, the **Recipient status**, **Failure and suppression reasons**, the **Version history** and the **Event timeline**. Under **Campaign controls**:

items: **Pause** and **Resume** stop and restart sending.
**Retry temporary failures** tries again for messages that failed for a passing reason.
**Cancel campaign** asks for a **Cancellation reason**. Messages not yet sent will not go out; messages already sent are not affected.
**Archive** puts away a finished or cancelled campaign.

rows: The QA checklist has errors, such as a missing objective, subject or content, an invalid link, or an unsupported merge field. Fix each and try again.
The person who submitted a campaign cannot approve it
Ask another reviewer to approve it.
Type the required changes before sending it back.
Scheduled time must be in the future
Pick a later date and time.
No eligible recipients match this audience
Nobody in the audience can receive this channel (for example no one has opted in or has an email address). Check the audience.
No temporary failures are eligible for retry

title: Campaigns: versioned audiences and consent
summary: Build reusable customer groups with include and exclude rules, preview who is in them, and understand how opt-outs are always respected.

body.text: **Marketing → Audiences** is where you build reusable groups of customers. You need permission to create and manage campaign audiences.

items: Click **New audience** and type the **Audience name**.
Under **Include contacts**, add conditions with **Add condition**, or a nested set with **Add group**. Choose **ALL** to match every condition or **ANY** to match at least one.
Under **Exclude contacts**, add anyone to leave out with **Add exclusion** or **Add exclusion group**. Anyone matching any exclusion is removed.
Click **Preview audience** to see how many match and a few **Sample matches**.
Click **Save audience** (or **Save new version** when editing).

body.text: Conditions can use: **Province**, **Lead source**, **Customer tag**, **Owns a vehicle**, **Vehicle model**, **Bought before**, **Service due**, **Lead status**, **Product interest**, **Customer created date**, **Has email address**, **Has phone / WhatsApp**, **Quote status** and **Customer value**.
**Marketing consent enforced**: deleted contacts and customers who opted out of marketing are always left out, whatever the rules say.

items: Every save creates a new version; **Saved audiences** shows each with its last calculated size.
**Edit**, **Duplicate** and **Archive** are on each saved audience. An archived audience can't be chosen for new campaigns; campaigns that already fixed their recipients keep them.
The preview uses today's data. When a campaign is queued or scheduled, the audience is worked out again and the recipient list is fixed.

body.text: Just before each message goes, the customer is checked again. Opt-outs, withdrawn consent, deleted contacts, missing email or phone details, sending limits and duplicates are recorded as **suppressed**, with the reason, rather than as delivery failures. They are listed under **Failure and suppression reasons** on the campaign.

items: **Give this audience a name before saving it.**: type the **Audience name**.
**No contacts currently match.**: loosen the conditions or check the exclusions.
**Historical audience criteria**: this audience was made with the old rules. Click **Replace** to rebuild it in the builder before changing it.

title: Campaigns: delivery, UTMs and attribution
summary: Read delivery, opens and clicks, set up link tracking, and understand how leads, quotes and sales are credited to a campaign.

body.text: Links in a campaign get the tracking tags you set under **2. Tracking and attribution** (**UTM source**, **medium**, **campaign**, **content** and **term**), so your website's analytics can tell where visitors came from. Tags already on a link are kept.

A campaign is credited with what happens after someone **clicks** a link in it: a new lead, a quote sent or accepted, or a won sale. It is **last click**: the most recent campaign clicked gets the credit, and only within the campaign's **Attribution window (days)**. Revenue counts only when there is a real value on the sale.

items: **ROAS** (return on ad spend) = revenue from credited won sales ÷ the campaign's budget.
**Cost per lead** = the campaign's budget ÷ credited leads.
Opens show interest only; they never earn credit.
Anything that happens outside the window isn't credited to the campaign.

body.text: Open counts are approximate: some email apps open every image automatically and others block them. Clicks, leads and sales are the more reliable measures.
Each campaign's page shows its recipients, delivery, engagement and conversions. **Marketing → Overview** adds them up across campaigns for a period.

title: Surveys: lifecycle, versions and governance
summary: How a survey goes from draft through review to a published version customers answer, and why a published survey can't be edited in place.

body.text: **Marketing → Surveys** holds your customer feedback forms. The figures at the top count **Drafts**, **In review**, **Approved** and **Published**. Working on surveys needs permission to create, send and manage surveys; viewing them and their responses needs permission to view surveys and responses.
Each survey is a **CSAT** (satisfaction), **Post-sale**, **NPS** (would you recommend us) or **Ad hoc** survey. The type decides how its scores are counted in Survey insights.

rows: New surveys always start here, switched off. Edit the questions.
Submitted. A reviewer approves it or requests changes with a note.
Customers can answer this version. It can be deactivated or archived.

items: The person who submitted a survey can't approve it.
Publishing freezes that version. To change a published survey, click **Create editable revision** and take the revision through review again.
Only one active survey can be sent automatically for each moment (job card completed, delivery completed, lead won).

title: Surveys: build, validate and publish
summary: Create a survey draft, set its questions and messages, take it through review, publish it and choose whether it is sent automatically.

items: On **Marketing → Surveys**, type a **New survey name**, choose its type and click **Create inactive draft**.
Open the survey and click **Edit questions** to set the introduction, thank-you message and questions.
Under **Lifecycle controls**, click **Submit for review**. Missing labels and answer options are refused at this point.
Another person clicks **Approve**, or types a **Required change note** and clicks **Request changes**.
Choose how it is sent: **Manual distribution**, or automatically when a **Job card completed**, **Delivery completed** or **Lead won**.
Add a **Version label (optional)** and click **Publish immutable version**.

body.text: If another active survey already uses that automatic moment, tick **Replace another active survey using this trigger** to take it over on purpose.
Invitations already sent keep showing the version they were sent with, even after you publish a newer one.

items: **Deactivate** stops the survey being sent.
**Create editable revision** starts a new draft from it.
**Archive** puts it away. **Published versions** lists every version.
**The person who submitted a survey cannot approve it**: ask someone else to approve.
**Changes requested:** at the top of the survey: read the note, make the changes and submit again.

title: Surveys: distributions, reminders and responses
summary: Send a published survey to a group of customers with reminders, follow its progress, and handle failed and suppressed invitations.

body.text: A distribution sends one published survey to a group of customers. Open **Survey distributions** with **Distribution queue** on **Marketing → Survey insights**, or **Create survey distribution** on the marketing calendar.

items: Under **Create a distribution**, type the **Distribution name**.
Choose the **Published survey** and the **Audience**: **All reachable contacts**, **Vehicle owners** or **Won customers**.
Choose the **Purpose**: **Transactional feedback** or **Marketing research**, and the **Channel**: **Best available**, **Email only** or **SMS only**.
Set the **Schedule**, **Reminder after hours** and **Maximum reminders**.
Click **Create queued distribution**.

body.text: Invitations go out in the background. Each customer is checked again just before sending: anyone who opted out or can't be reached is recorded as suppressed rather than failed.

items: **Pause** and **Resume** stop and restart sending.
**Retry permanent failures** tries again for invitations that failed.
**Cancel remaining** asks you to confirm: invites not yet sent will not go out; invites already delivered are not affected.
**Failures and suppressions** lists each problem with its reason and attempts, keeping consent blocks separate from delivery failures.
**Publish a survey first.**: there is no published survey to send.
**Many suppressed invitations**: these customers opted out or have no email or mobile number. Check their contact details.

title: Survey insights and closed-loop recovery
summary: Read response rate, NPS and CSAT correctly, and follow up unhappy customers through the recovery queue.

body.text: **Marketing → Survey insights** shows how your surveys are doing. Narrow it by survey, distribution, type and channel, then click **Apply**.

rows: Completed responses as a share of invitations actually delivered. Invitations that failed or were suppressed don't count.
The percentage of promoters (9–10) minus the percentage of detractors (0–6). **NPS composition** shows the promoters, passives (7–8) and detractors.
The percentage of CSAT and post-sale scores rated 4 or 5.
How long customers took to answer, from when the invitation was delivered.

body.text: **Daily response trend** shows delivered, completed, response rate and average score per day. **Recent responses** lists each answer with its score and comment.
A low NPS or CSAT score creates a follow-up in the **Closed-loop recovery queue** automatically. For each one:

items: Choose a team member and click **Assign**.
Type **How was this resolved?** and click **Resolve follow-up**, or
Click **Create support case** to open a case with the customer, the score and their comment.

body.text: Working the queue needs permission to create, send and manage surveys.

title: Marketing overview and calendar
summary: See campaign results, attributed revenue and survey health for a period, and every scheduled campaign and survey send on one calendar.

body.text: **Marketing → Overview** totals your marketing for a period. Set the **Reporting window** (**From** and to) and click **Apply period**; every figure on the page uses it.

items: **Campaign activity**: campaigns and messages delivered.
**Attributed outcomes**: leads, quotes and sales credited to campaigns.
**Attributed revenue**: revenue from credited sales, with ROAS when a budget is set.
**Engagement**: clicks, with cost per lead when a budget is set.
**Top attributable campaigns**: each campaign's status, clicks, conversions, revenue and ROAS.

body.text: **Marketing → Calendar** shows scheduled campaign launches and survey distributions on one monthly calendar. Use **Month** and **Type** (**Campaigns and surveys**, **Campaigns** or **Surveys**) to focus it, and **Previous** / **Next** to move between months. Click an item to open it.
